messages:
noah: quick note from trying to onboard a new engineer: our Go generator iterator API is awkward when the HTTP handler needs to cancel mid-stream. we hit two UX gaps: 1) iter.Next() keeps returning tokens after the parent req ctx is canceled because internal retry/auth uses background ctx; 2) there's no simple way to signal "shutdown now" from user code other than closing the parent connection. felt clunky.

amelia: can you sketch the flow you used? interesting we keep getting subtle leaks in sampleapps.

noah: simplified handler:
```go
func GenHandler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    iter := sdk.Generator("redwood-mini").Stream(r.Context(), Prompt{Text: "build me"})
    for iter.Next() {
        chunk := iter.Text()
        if _, err := w.Write([]byte(chunk)); err != nil {
            // client gone -> want to stop the stream
            log.Println("write failed", err)
            return
        }
    }
    if err := iter.Err(); err != nil {
        log.Println("iter err", err)
    }
}
```

jin: yeah this is pretty typical. the subtle bit is the SDK's background token refresher that can recreate transport with a root background ctx. once created the iterator believes it's still live. we fixed several cases by threading ctx through refresh, but that doesn't help when user code wants to proactively tear down the iterator without canceling the entire request context.

amelia: why not just cancel request ctx? sometimes you want to keep the request alive for cleanup or metrics after shutting generator down. also, the handler above returns on write error but there's still a goroutine inside iter that may be blocked in transport read.

noah: exactly. proposal: add an explicit method on the iterator such as Close() or Cancel() which will synchronously request transport shutdown and drain resources. semantics: Close() is idempotent, causes Next() to return false soon, and Err() returns context.Canceled or a sentinel ErrClosed. also provide example in README.

jin: I like an explicit Close. alternatives: accept a context on Next/Receive which is more invasive. Close() is easier opt-in. but need to design to avoid races: Next() may block waiting for network, Close() must unblock it. for net/http based transport we can call conn.Close() under the hood; for gRPC/HTTP2 we might need to cancel stream ctx.

amelia: thoughts on naming? Close vs Cancel vs Stop? Close aligns with io.Closer but ErrClosed might confuse. Cancel communicates intent more clearly. we could implement Close() and deprecate it later if needed.

jin: API sketch:
```go
type GeneratorIter interface {
    Next() bool
    Text() string
    Err() error
    Close() error // synchronous
}
```
Close should accept context? Close(ctx) could be nicer to bound wait time. maybe Close(context.Context) so callers can set a timeout.

noah: Right. Close(ctx) gives users deterministic teardown inside request handlers. Proposed semantics in README snippet plus example handler accepting Close on write failure.

docs-bot: reminder: update Go SDK README and sampleapps if we change API. run a quick grep for Generator().Stream(...).Stream(ctx) usages across repo.

qa-bot: can we add a unit + integration test: unit to ensure Close unblocks Next; integration to simulate midstream auth refresh + Close while server still sending. I can add a harness.

jin: implementation note: our lower-level transport currently uses a read loop that pushes events into a channel consumed by Next(). We can close that channel from Close() and also cancel the transport ctx. need to ensure no double-close panics.

amelia: backward-compat: add Close(ctx) but keep existing iterator types so no break. bump minor semver. also add a small deprecation note: "If you previously relied on canceling parent ctx for stream shutdown, prefer iterator.Close(ctx) for predictable teardown."

noah: i'll draft a PR with the API surface, a small shim that wires Close to existing transport cancellation, and update two sampleapps to use Close on write failure. will include unit test that uses net.Pipe to emulate server that keeps sending after Close; assert Next returns false quickly.

jin: +1. please also include a doc snippet explaining why Context.Background() inside SDK internals is dangerous and recommend passing a parent ctx or using Close for explicit teardown.

amelia: thanks. this should reduce a lot of onboarding confusion where new devs expect request cancel automatically stops all work. small follow-up: can we add a linter check in sampleapps that flags Context.Background() use in network/auth code paths? could be a low-friction docs/automation win.

noah: good idea. I'll add a TODO in the PR referencing docs lint. PR link when ready. :rocket:
